$comment: The tunables, declared once. Two stacks read this file — the Node services through libs/common/src/settings.ts and the Python admin through apps/admin/registry.py — so a knob is added here and appears in both, with the same bounds and the same default. It is data rather than code precisely because neither stack should own it.

groups.label: Sync cadence
groups.about: How often a wallet is rescanned. This is the top of the funnel: everything below it only decides how the work already asked for gets done.

groups.label: Throughput
groups.about: How fast the work is handed out once it is due. Turning these up costs upstream rate limits, not our own CPU.

groups.label: Timeouts and give-up
groups.about: When a scan stops being slow and starts being lost.

settings.label: EVM balances
settings.about: debank scrapes a page in a headless browser: ~6s, and an IP budget a few dozen wallets exhaust. zerion is an API: ~0.4s, no ban risk, needs ZERION_API_KEY on scanner-evm.

settings.label: Portfolios in use
settings.about: The real pacing knob: the queue only takes addresses that are due, so this — not scan speed — sets the load.
settings.note: Read by three services. The api marks a wallet stale at 3× this and reports it to the browser, so this being one value in one place is the point.

settings.label: Portfolios nobody opens
settings.about: Anonymous or signed-in makes no difference — only whether somebody has opened it.

settings.label: Goes stale after
settings.about: How long somebody can be away before their portfolio drops to the slow interval.

settings.label: Queue top-up
settings.about: How often the producer looks for addresses that have come due. Cheap: an address that is not due is not enqueued.

settings.label: Addresses per scanner
settings.about: How many at once. Raising it multiplies the request rate against the same upstream sources, which is what earns a 429.

settings.label: Pause after each scan
settings.about: The pacing knob against DeBank. The scanner holds its queue slot for the whole pause.
settings.note: The scanner service has no database and cannot pick this up live; it applies there on the next deploy. The wallet service's own in-process loop reads it live.

settings.label: Parallel requests per scan
settings.about: Inside one BTC, SOL or TRON scan. Separate from how many scans run at all.

settings.label: Scan lease
settings.about: How long an address is believed to be in flight before it counts as free again.

settings.label: Retry after a failure
settings.about: Keeps somebody else's outage from becoming our own rate limit.

settings.label: HTTP scan timeout
settings.about: Per request in the BTC, SOL and TRON scanners.

settings.label: EVM scan timeout
settings.about: A browser scan is slow by nature: a page load with chains resolving one by one.

settings.label: Alert events at once
settings.about: How many wallet-state events the collector works through in parallel. The work is a couple of queries.
settings.note: A consumer's prefetch is fixed when it subscribes, so this one takes effect on the next deploy of monitor-alerts.

rules.about: The scan lease must outlast the slowest scan it covers, or an address is dispatched a second time while the first is still running.
The interval for portfolios nobody opens cannot be shorter than the one for portfolios in use — that would scan the forgotten ones more often than the watched ones.
